Bonaparte’s Retreat, X:2

A friend presented me with this tune last week as she had been given it to learn.
She had misgivings about the correctness of the transcription and because I was unfamiliar with this version of “Bonaparte’retreat” so I watched the clip of Ali Bain playing it in group. Hope someone finds it useful.
I used www.mandolintab.net/abcconverter.php to check my accuracy. I have used Concertina.net in the past but that seems unavailable now. It is worth checking before submitting and is a very useful way to help the learning process.
I shall now contemplate the ‘Old Timey’ versions.

Re: Bonaparte’s Retreat

Alan Lomax recorded Kentucky fiddler W. H. Stepp () in 1937 for the Library of Congress.
In 1941 he published his book Our Singing Country in which a score of Stepp’s performance appeared (it was transcribed by Peggy Seeger’s mother Ruth Crawford Seeger).
Copland’s ‘Hoe-Down’ is the last part of his Ballet ‘Rodeo’, premiered in 1942 and is made up of several bits of Irish tunes (including Gilderoy (fr. 2‘17“ in the video), besides Miss McLeod (fr. 2’08” as has been noted) set along with the more typically American ‘Bonyparte’. Interestingly, the farsighted choreographer Agnes de Mille insisted that the tunes should be orchestrated as little as possible. The result was a great success.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v40IjawyW2k
I’m not sure who today wouldn’t prefer Stepp’s version, by a mile, to Copland’s.
William H. Stepp’s sound was in many ways more subtle than the classical composer’s score (or, at least, to the classical musicians‘ phrasing style) and his sound was no less ’big’ for that: it is reported he could play, singly, for balls numbering 300 people.

Bonaparte’s Retreat, X:4

This is as near to Aly Bains version as I can get.I had to change the 2/4 bar in A and B part as it was mucking up the notes lower down on this system , but I think musically it sounds the same the way I did it. Some players only play the B part twice , not 3 times. Its up to you.
Comments /assistance welcome.

Re: Bonaparte’s Retreat

I have re edited X4 and seemed to have removed the glitch and now it has the 2/4 bars installed and everything is good.I have used The playing of Aly Bain and Phil Cunningham as the basis for this setting. There are differences in the version on Transatlantic Sessions and the Bain/Cunningham version.Firstly , in Transatlantic the B part ( Line 3) is played 3 times , whereas in the other it is played 4 times, as I have notated. Second difference is that the order of some parts are reversed , ie what I call part C , A and B parts are reversed in the latter part of the tune.
